correctness.rationale: Two wild poles of order 3 give genus three by Artin–Schreier Riemann–Hurwitz. The Klein four involutions yield genus-one quotient y²+y=t³+t and genus-two complementary quotient z²+z=t³+t+t^(-1), with rational full quotient, so Kani–Rosen character idempotents split the Jacobian isogeny. The F2, F4, F8 trace counts (N1,N2,N3)=(4,8,4) determine the first three Hasse–Weil coefficients via Newton identities; the genus-three functional equation determines the remaining coefficients, factoring into (1+2T+2T²)(1-2T+2T²)(1+T+2T²). The corresponding elliptic Frobenius traces -2,+2,-1 are valid by explicit elliptic models and Tate. Verified independently via finite-field bit arithmetic and polynomial multiplication; supplemental n=4..6 counts in package are consistency checks, not infinite sampling.
